(CSXT) petition for relief from certain regulations concerning inspections performed by qualified mechanical inspectors (QMIs).","publishedAt":"2026-11-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22335","title":"Notice of Petition for Waiver of Compliance","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/02/2026-22335/notice-of-petition-for-waiver-of-compliance","summary":"This document extends the period for public comment regarding the Union Pacific Railroad Company (UPRR) petition for relief from certain regulations concerning inspections performed by qualified mechanical inspectors (QMIs).","publishedAt":"2026-11-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22331","title":"Notice of Final Federal Agency Actions on Transportation Project in Nebraska","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/02/2026-22331/notice-of-final-federal-agency-actions-on-transportation-project-in-nebraska","summary":"This notice announces actions taken by the FHWA, on behalf of the Nebraska Department of Transportation and Iowa Department of Transportation, that are final. The action(s) relate to the Decatur Bridge Project, located in Burt County, Nebraska and Monona County, Iowa. Those actions grant licenses, permits, and approvals for the project. The project involves improving the existing Nebraska Highway 51 (N-51)/Iowa Highway 175 (IA-175) crossing of the Missouri River near Decatur, Nebraska. The FHWA's National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) provides details on the Selected Alternative for the proposed improvements.","publishedAt":"2026-11-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22318","title":"Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/02/2026-22318/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report that, during production, certain sealant installations within the center wing fuel tank did not receive required visual and adhesion inspections. This AD requires a detailed inspection of certain sealant installations in the left, right, and center wing side-of-body areas, an adhesion test of the sealant, and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22317","title":"Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/02/2026-22317/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes","summary":"The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2023-07- 09, which applied to certain The Boeing Company Model 747-400 and -8 series airplanes. AD 2023-07-09 required inspecting for wear of the transfer pump housing inlet check valves and transfer pump motor impeller inlet adapters for the horizontal stabilizer fuel tank and doing corrective actions, if necessary, and limited the installation of affected parts. This AD was prompted by the manufacturer developing further action to address the unsafe condition. This AD requires repetitive inspections for damage of the transfer pump housing inlet check valves and transfer pump motor impeller inlet adapters for the horizontal stabilizer fuel tank and applicable on-condition actions. This AD also limits the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22310","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Diamond Aircraft Industries Inc. Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/02/2026-22310/airworthiness-directives-diamond-aircraft-industries-inc-airplanes","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Diamond Aircraft Industries Inc. (DAI) Model DA 40, DA 40 F, and DA 40 NG airplanes. This AD was prompted by several reports of passenger door separation during flight. This AD requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) to provide the flight crew with revised operating limitations, emergency procedures, and normal operating procedures; inspecting the passenger door latching mechanism and safety hook mechanism areas and performing corrective action, as applicable; inspecting the safety hook, latching bolts, front and rear door guide blocks, canopy and passenger door warning light, carbon hinges, tension spring, retaining block, safety hook push button, latching mechanism spring, gas spring, and door frame; measuring the passenger door handle actuation force; modifying the airplane with placards; replacing the gas spring; and replacing the hook assembly, retaining block, door guide blocks, and door sealant if necessary. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22307","title":"Airworthiness Directives; BRP-Rotax GmbH & Co KG (Formerly BRP-Powertrain GMBH & CO KG and Bombardier-Rotax GmbH) Engines","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/02/2026-22307/airworthiness-directives-brp-rotax-gmbh-and-co-kg-formerly-brp-powertrain-gmbh-and-co-kg-and","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all BRP-Rotax GmbH & Co KG (BRP-Rotax) Model 915 iSc2 C24, 915 iSc3 C24, 916 iSc2 A, 916 iSc2 C24, 916 iSc3 A, and 916 iSc3 C24 engines. This AD was prompted by a report of oil leakage from cracks in the wall of the turbocharger valve housing due to insufficient thickness. This AD requires replacement of the turbocharger valve housing and reidentification of the turbocharger. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22277","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities; Renewal of an Approved Information Collection Request: Hazardous Materials Safety Permits","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/02/2026-22277/agency-information-collection-activities-renewal-of-an-approved-information-collection-request","summary":"In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FMCSA announces its plan to submit the Information Collection Request (ICR) described below to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval. This ICR requires companies holding safety permits to develop communications plans that allow for the periodic tracking of the shipments. A record of communications that includes the time of the call and location of the shipment may be kept by either the driver (e.g., recorded in the logbook) or the company. These records must be kept, either physically or electronically, for at least 6 months at the company's principal place of business or readily available to the employees at the company's principal place of business. No comments were received in response to the 60-day Federal Register notice.","publishedAt":"2026-11-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22242","title":"Notice of Meeting of the National Parks Overflights Advisory Group","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/30/2026-22242/notice-of-meeting-of-the-national-parks-overflights-advisory-group","summary":"The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the National Park Service (NPS), in accordance with the National Parks Air Tour Management Act of 2000 (NPATMA), announce the next meeting of the National Parks Overflights Advisory Group (NPOAG). This notification provides the date, location, and agenda for the meeting.","publishedAt":"2026-10-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22226","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission to the Office of Management and Budget for Review and Approval; Request for Comment; State Data Transfer (SDT)","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/30/2026-22226/agency-information-collection-activities-submission-to-the-office-of-management-and-budget-for","summary":"In compliance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), this notice announces that the Information Collection Request (ICR) summarized below will be submitted to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval. The ICR describes the nature of the information collection and its expected burden. This document describes a collection of information for which NHTSA intends to seek OMB approval on the State Data Transfer (SDT) program for Vehicle Crash Information. A Federal Register Notice with a 60-day comment period soliciting comments on this information collection was published on June 25, 2026. NHTSA received one public comment.","publishedAt":"2026-10-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22223","title":"Standard Instrument Approach Procedures, and Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures; Miscellaneous Amendments","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/30/2026-22223/standard-instrument-approach-procedures-and-takeoff-minimums-and-obstacle-departure-procedures","summary":"This rule amends, suspends, or removes Standard Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPs) and associated Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures for operations at certain airports. These regulatory actions are needed because of the adoption of new or revised criteria, or because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System, such as the commissioning of new navigational facilities, adding new obstacles, or changing air traffic requirements. These changes are designed to provide for the safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace and to promote safe flight operations under instrument flight rules at the affected airports.","publishedAt":"2026-10-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22222","title":"Standard Instrument Approach Procedures, and Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures; Miscellaneous Amendments","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/30/2026-22222/standard-instrument-approach-procedures-and-takeoff-minimums-and-obstacle-departure-procedures","summary":"This rule establishes, amends, suspends, or removes Standard Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPS) and associated Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure procedures (ODPs) for operations at certain airports. These regulatory actions are needed because of the adoption of new or revised criteria, or because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System, such as the commissioning of new navigational facilities, adding new obstacles, or changing air traffic requirements. These changes are designed to provide safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace and to promote safe flight operations under instrument flight rules at the affected airports.","publishedAt":"2026-10-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22197","title":"Amendment of Class D and Establishment of Class E Airspace; Chandler and Phoenix, AZ","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/30/2026-22197/amendment-of-class-d-and-establishment-of-class-e-airspace-chandler-and-phoenix-az","summary":"This action amends the Class D airspace and establishes Class E airspace at Chandler and Phoenix, AZ. This action is the result of biennial airspace reviews pursuant to FAA Order JO 7400.2R, Procedures for Handling Airspace Matters. The name and geographic coordinates of the Mesa Gateway Airport, Phoenix, AZ, are also being updated to coincide with the FAA's aeronautical database. This action brings the airspace into compliance with FAA orders and supports instrument flight rule (IFR) procedures and operations.","publishedAt":"2026-10-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22168","title":"Safety Advisory 26-01 Overhead Catenary System (OCS) and Pantograph Reliability","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/30/2026-22168/safety-advisory-26-01-overhead-catenary-system-ocs-and-pantograph-reliability","summary":"The Federal Transit Administration (FTA) is issuing Safety Advisory 26-01 to recommend State Safety Oversight Agencies (SSOAs) direct Rail Transit Agencies (RTAs) within their jurisdiction to use their Safety Management System (SMS) to identify hazards and mitigate risks related to Overhead Catenary System (OCS) and pantograph failures.","publishedAt":"2026-10-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22125","title":"Denial of Motor Vehicle Defect Petition, DP26-009","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/30/2026-22125/denial-of-motor-vehicle-defect-petition-dp26-009","summary":"This notice sets forth the reasons for the denial of defect petition (DP26-009) submitted by Mr. Jason Rund (petitioner) to NHTSA's Administrator. The petition requests NHTSA (the Agency) to initiate a defect investigation to determine if an issue with the rear differential (final drive) assembly of 2022 BMW 540i vehicles is causing the rear wheels to decouple from the drivetrain. Following a technical review of the petition and other information, NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) concluded that that the issues raised do not warrant a defect investigation at this time. Accordingly, the Agency has denied the petition.","publishedAt":"2026-10-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22098","title":"Notice of Intent To Rule on a Land Release Request for Disposal of Airport Property at the Fairbanks International Airport, Fairbanks, AK","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/29/2026-22098/notice-of-intent-to-rule-on-a-land-release-request-for-disposal-of-airport-property-at-the-fairbanks","summary":"Notice is being given that the FAA is considering a request from the Fairbanks International Airport to release 40 (<plus-minus>) acres of federally obligated airport property at the Fairbanks International Airport, Fairbanks, Alaska. This acreage was acquired with federal financial assistance via Airport Improvement Program Federal Grants. The release of property will allow the Fairbanks International Airport to dispose of the property for non-aeronautical purposes.","publishedAt":"2026-10-29","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22095","title":"Notice of Intent To Rule on a Land Release Request for Disposal of Airport Property at the Kingman Airport, Kingman, AZ","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/29/2026-22095/notice-of-intent-to-rule-on-a-land-release-request-for-disposal-of-airport-property-at-the-kingman","summary":"Notice is being given that the FAA is considering a request from the City of Kingman to release 832.6 (+/-) acres of federally obligated airport property at the Kingman Airport (IGM), Kingman, AZ. This acreage was obtained from the United States Government under the Surplus Property Act of 1944. The release of property will allow the City of Kingman to dispose of the property for non-aeronautical purposes.","publishedAt":"2026-10-29","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22069","title":"Proposed Agency Information Collection Activities; Comment Request","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/29/2026-22069/proposed-agency-information-collection-activities-comment-request","summary":"Under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA) and its implementing regulations, this notice announces that FRA is forwarding the Information Collection Request (ICR) summarized below to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and comment. The ICR describes the information collection and its expected burden. On August 14, 2026, FRA published a notice providing a 60-day period for public comment on the ICR. FRA received one comment in response to the notice.","publishedAt":"2026-10-29","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22068","title":"Proposed Agency Information Collection Activities; Comment Request","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/29/2026-22068/proposed-agency-information-collection-activities-comment-request","summary":"Under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA) and its implementing regulations, this notice announces that FRA is forwarding the Information Collection Request (ICR) summarized below to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and comment. The ICR describes the information collection and its expected burden. On August 14, 2026, FRA published a notice providing a 60-day period for public comment on the ICR. FRA received two comments in response to the notice.","publishedAt":"2026-10-29","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22067","title":"NHTSA Workshop on Aftermarket Modifications and ADAS Performance","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/29/2026-22067/nhtsa-workshop-on-aftermarket-modifications-and-adas-performance","summary":"The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) will hold a Workshop on December 10, 2026 to use its convening authority to discuss advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) performance, as it pertains to the effects of aftermarket modifications. The event will not be live streamed; however, it will be recorded and made available on the NHTSA website after the event.","publishedAt":"2026-10-29","source":"Federal Register"}]}
